name: Jupiter
lede: A hydrogen–helium storm world with a centuries-old Great Red Spot and a family of Galilean moons.

landmark.label: Great Red Spot
landmark.blurb: A persistent high-pressure storm in the southern hemisphere, observed for centuries and still larger than Earth.

missions.name: Pioneer 10 & 11
missions.note: First flybys through the outer solar system.

missions.name: Voyager 1 & 2
missions.note: Detailed imaging of belts, the Red Spot, and the Galilean moons.

missions.name: Juno
missions.note: Polar orbiter mapping gravity, magnetosphere, and deep atmosphere.

researchNotes: Jupiter is the most massive planet. Its rapid rotation flattens the globe and drives strong zonal winds that paint the familiar belts and zones.
The Great Red Spot is an anticyclone. It has shrunk over the last century but remains a defining feature of the southern hemisphere.
Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto — the Galilean moons — are worlds in their own right: volcanoes, subsurface oceans, and ancient cratered crusts.
folklore: Named for the king of Roman gods. Astrology's Jupiter is symbolism; the storm and moons are spacecraft fact.
carlFocus: Lead with the Great Red Spot, fast spin, and Galilean moons. Mention Voyager and Juno when asked about exploration.
